lines: Registrations exceeded what three doctors can see in 1 hour(s) (starting 09:00; peak load 1.16 × capacity), so a queue built up.
Both algorithms called every patient in the same order, so every waiting-time result is identical: in this workload WRR's rotation never had to choose differently from WPS-A.
Priority-lane violations: WPS-A 0, WRR 0. WRR did not need to call a Regular ahead of a waiting Senior/PWD/Pregnant patient in this run.

Aging cap: 4 Regular patient(s) waited 20 minutes or more under WPS-A (bonus capped at +2); they were bypassed 2 more time(s) after reaching the cap. A Regular's effective priority stops at 3, so it can never pass a waiting Senior, PWD or Pregnant patient; the cap limits reordering, not waiting time.
Throughput 13.51 vs 13.51 patients/hour and mean utilization 66.6% vs 66.6%: both algorithms keep every free doctor busy, so capacity is not what separates them.

criteria.label: Bounded waiting for Regular patients (no starvation)
criteria.why: A Regular patient must eventually be seen even on a day with many Vulnerable registrations.

criteria.label: Average waiting time
criteria.why: Matters for overall satisfaction, but averages can hide a few very long waits.

criteria.label: Throughput and doctor utilization
criteria.why: Both algorithms keep every free doctor busy whenever someone waits, so these are expected to match; a difference only reflects which consultation lengths ended last.
